subject.title: Telegram owner commands: trusted execution mode for approval-gated actions

question: Should OpenClaw add a trusted-owner approval-bypass mode for Telegram group-origin privileged actions, and should that live as a shared approval/elevated/tool-class policy rather than a Telegram-only boolean?
rationale: Source and release inspection show the requested mode is absent, but deciding when an operator identity may skip approvals changes a security boundary and config contract that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design shared trusted-owner policy
options.body: Add a disabled-by-default policy with explicit sender, allowlisted group, tool-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics across the existing approval stack.

options.title: Keep existing approval model
options.body: Decline the bypass and document that operators who want no prompts must use existing permissive exec/elevated policy with clear security tradeoffs.

options.title: Add Telegram-only shortcut
options.body: Implement the proposed Telegram config directly, accepting a narrower patch with higher long-term risk of approval-policy drift.

recommendation.title: Design shared trusted-owner policy
recommendation.body: Add a disabled-by-default policy with explicit sender, allowlisted group, tool-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics across the existing approval stack.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans product policy, security defaults, and config-surface direction before Telegram and approval owners can implement safely.
